title: Objects of $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ descend to a finite extension
statement:
Let $X$ be a standing scheme [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and fix the prime $\ell$ and algebraic closure $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use the bounded constructible categories $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude], with the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings, not constant discrete rational coefficient sheaves. All finite fields below are intermediate fields of $\Qlb/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Write $C_F=T_{E,F}C$ and $C_{\Qlb}=T_{E,\Qlb}C$ for the derived extensions of scalars [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield, def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar]. Here these functors act on unbounded derived categories of module objects in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$; in particular $T_{E,\Qlb}$ is the coefficient-change functor for the condensed inclusion $\underline E\to\underline{\Qlb}$, as specified by [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar].

For every $K\in\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ there are a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $K_E\in\Dbc(X,E)$ with $(K_E)_{\Qlb}\cong K$. If $K_E$ is such a model over $E$ and $E\subseteq F\subseteq\Qlb$ is finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, then $(K_E)_F\in\Dbc(X,F)$ and $((K_E)_F)_{\Qlb}\cong K$, so $(K_E)_F$ is a model over $F$.

proof.text: Check the geometric hypotheses used below. The standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] makes $X$ separated and of finite type over a field $k$. Since $k$ has only the ideals $0,k$, $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives that $X$ is Noetherian. Its locally closed strata $S$ are qcqs: locally their rings are quotients of localizations of Noetherian rings, and their underlying spaces are Noetherian. Thus $S$, and every intersection of two affine opens of $S$, are quasi-compact (an open cover of a Noetherian space has a finite subcover, by stabilization of finite unions). This verifies the qcqs hypothesis when lisse descent is applied on $S$, and the Noetherian hypothesis when finite generation and triangulated closure are applied on $X$.

source.place: Preliminary verification of the hypotheses of the Sheaves and Complexes paragraphs; Morphisms Lemma 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian).

proof.text: Models persist and may be shifted. For $E\subseteq F$, [lem-sfb-extend-subfield-constructible] gives $(K_E)_F\in\Dbc(X,F)$, and [def-sfb-derived-extend-comp-iso] gives $((K_E)_F)_{\Qlb}\cong(K_E)_{\Qlb}\cong K$. This proves the second assertion. The functor $T_{E,\Qlb}$ is the left derived extension on the module-object categories over the pulled-back condensed rings, exactly as specified by the current [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar]; its additional identification with condensed coefficient change uses the same inclusion. The scalar-extension functors to a finite field and to $\Qlb$ are computed termwise, preserve distinguished triangles and commute with every shift: apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the flat scalar extensions of [lem-sfb-subfield-flat] and [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat]. Exactness here follows from preservation of finite limits together with right exactness of extension of scalars, which is a tensor left adjoint by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] identifies the left derived extensions just defined with these termwise functors; thus the triangle and shift comparisons apply to the specified $T_{E,F}$ and $T_{E,\Qlb}$. Thus $K_E[n]$ models $K[n]$; it is bounded constructible by [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-triangulated]. For two finite fields $E_1,E_2$, their finite compositum $E_1E_2$ exists by [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], and the just-proved persistence puts two models over a common field.

source.place: Models persist paragraph, with exactness and shift compatibility spelled out; Stacks Derived Categories Lemmas 015F and 014X.

proof.text: Descent is closed under extensions. Suppose $A\to K\to B\xrightarrow{\delta}A[1]$ is distinguished and $A,B$ have bounded constructible models. By step 2, put them over a common finite $E$ and fix isomorphisms $\alpha:(A_E)_{\Qlb}\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ and $\beta:(B_E)_{\Qlb}\xrightarrow{\sim}B$. The transported map $\alpha[1]^{-1}\circ\delta\circ\beta:(B_E)_{\Qlb}\to(A_E)_{\Qlb}[1]$ is represented at some finite $F\supseteq E$ by $\delta_F:(B_E)_F\to(A_E)_F[1]$: use the surjectivity in [det-lem-coefficient-finite-descent-hom] (3) with $C=B_E$, $D=A_E$, $r=1$. An element of this filtered colimit has a representative at one finite stage. Write $A_F=(A_E)_F$ and $B_F=(B_E)_F$. By TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], complete $\delta_F$ to a distinguished triangle $B_F\xrightarrow{\delta_F}A_F[1]\xrightarrow{v_F}C_F\xrightarrow{w_F}B_F[1]$ and put $K_F=C_F[-1]$. Applying the inverse rotation of TR2 once gives $C_F[-1]\xrightarrow{-w_F[-1]}B_F\xrightarrow{\delta_F}A_F[1]\xrightarrow{v_F}C_F$; applying it again gives $A_F\xrightarrow{-v_F[-1]}K_F\xrightarrow{-w_F[-1]}B_F\xrightarrow{\delta_F}A_F[1]$. In particular the connecting arrow is $\delta_F$, with no sign change. The two endpoints lie in $\Dbc(X,F)$ by step 2, so $K_F$ does too by [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-triangulated]. Apply the exact scalar extension of step 2. Rotate this triangle and the given triangle until their first arrows are respectively $(\delta_F)_{\Qlb}$ and $\delta$. By construction $\beta$ and $\alpha[1]$ form a commuting square on these first arrows; TR3 completes it to a morphism of distinguished triangles. Its third component is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], and rotating back gives $(K_F)_{\Qlb}\cong K$. In particular, if $u:A\to B$ is any morphism between descended objects, its cone descends: rotate $A\to B\to\operatorname{Cone}(u)\to A[1]$ to the extension triangle $B\to\operatorname{Cone}(u)\to A[1]\to B[1]$ and apply the result just proved.

source.place: Cones paragraph; the TR3 comparison and the passage from extensions to cones are made explicit.

proof.text: The generators have models. Let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ be locally closed, $L$ a lisse $\Qlb_S$-module, and $n\in\mathbf Z$. By step 1, $S$ is qcqs. Part (1) of [det-lem-coefficient-finite-descent-lisse], applied on $S$, supplies a finite $E$ and a lisse $E_S$-module $L_E$ with $(L_E)_{\Qlb}\cong L$. Put $G_E=a_!L_E[n]$. The converse assertion of [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation], for $\Lambda=E$, says that this generator is in $\Dbc(X,E)$. The identification in [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar], on both $S$ and $X$, makes $T_{E,\Qlb}$ the coefficient change for the same condensed inclusion $\underline E\to\underline{\Qlb}$. Consequently part (2) of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] gives $(a_!L_E)_{\Qlb}\cong a_!((L_E)_{\Qlb})$. Combining it with the shift compatibility of step 2 and the chosen lisse isomorphism gives $(G_E)_{\Qlb}\cong a_!L[n]$. This uses extension by zero for a locally closed immersion, including its closed factor; an open-immersion comparison alone would not suffice.

proof.text: Finish by a finite induction, with no infinite passage of coefficient fields. Apply [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation] for $\Lambda=\Qlb$ to $K$. It supplies a finite sequence $K_1,\ldots,K_N=K$, each term a generator $a_!L[n]$ or isomorphic to a cone between earlier terms, up to shift. Induct on the sequence index: a generator has the model of step 4; a cone has a model by step 3 after putting its two earlier models over a common finite field by step 2; a shift has the shifted model by step 2. An isomorphism to such an object is handled by composing the model isomorphism. The zero object has the zero model over $\mathbf Q_\ell$ (and can also be taken as a rank-zero lisse generator). There are only finitely many induction steps, each choosing one finite extension or one finite compositum, so the final model $K_E$ is over a finite extension. The finite-generation lemma packages exactly the source's finite sheaf filtration followed by the finite cohomological truncation induction; its statement supplies the entire finite sequence, rather than requiring access to its proof.
